# Orkas **An open-source team of AI agents on your desktop — it turns your goals into finished work and keeps it moving.** Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app — an AI assistant that works as a team. Tell the **Commander** what you need: it finishes many tasks on its own, and for bigger work it plans the steps and brings in specialist agents along with the coding and personal agents you already use — **Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent** — to work on it together. Orkas is built to keep a project moving, not just answer one prompt. A **project** holds the goal, rules, memory and files, so every new conversation picks up where the last one left off. **To-dos** split the work between people and agents, **Auto-advance** lets the team take on the next to-do by itself, and **scheduled automations** repeat routine work hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. All your data stays on your computer, and finished work comes back for your review — so you can trust Orkas with the ongoing work of your business. **[⬇ Download Orkas for macOS & Windows](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** — free, with 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model, so you don't need an API key to start. Prefer your own keys? Claude · OpenAI · Gemini · DeepSeek · Kimi · GLM · Qwen · MiniMax · Doubao, or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Browse 30+ agents in the [agent marketplace](https://orkas.ai/views/marketplace/gs/agents/?source=gh-orkas), or describe the role you need and the Commander builds a custom agent for you.

### Recreate a reference video with your own content **VideoStudio** can recreate a viral video's narrative structure, visual style and editing pace using your own product, script and footage. Supply a reference video file and your assets: the agent analyzes the hook, information order, visual beats and call to action, then proposes what to preserve and what to replace before production. This works best for motion-graphic explainers, SaaS or app demos, and product ads built from your existing footage. Locally authored text, captions, narration and clips can be revised separately; text baked into AI-generated footage requires changing that footage. > "Use reference.mp4 as a reference for a 30-second vertical promo. Keep its hook, typography and pacing, replace the content with my product and screen recordings, and show me the breakdown and plan first." Start with a video file the agent can read; social-platform share-link downloading is not built in. Exact camera moves, human performances and frame-by-frame matching are not guaranteed. See the [reference-recreation workflow](./resources/builtin/marketplace/agents/79df9cc89f5f/skills/video-craft/references/reference-recreation.md). --- ## Keep the work moving One task is a good start. Orkas is built for the work that keeps going. - **Projects** — goals & rules, memory and files that every conversation in the project starts from, so you never brief from scratch. - **To-dos and Auto-advance** — every project has a to-do list for people and agents; with Auto-advance on, the team picks up the next item on its own and brings finished work back for your review. - **Scheduled automations** — run any task hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. Orkas runs on your computer. From v1.9, each automation catches up its most recent missed run within 12 hours when the computer wakes or Orkas starts. - **Connectors** — Gmail, Google Calendar, Sheets and Drive, Notion, Slack, Shopify, Stripe and many more. By default, Orkas asks before it sends, posts or deletes anything. - **Apps** — describe a tool and Orkas builds it as a local app inside the desktop app. In the packaged app, paid plans can also publish it as a web app with a public link. - **Shared projects** *(packaged app)* — invite a teammate or VA, and give each to-do to a person or an agent. > [!NOTE] > Shared projects, cloud sync and web-app publishing are only in the packaged app — the open-source build doesn't support them yet. To use them, **[download Orkas for macOS & Windows](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** (free, with 500 credits to start). Voice input also works in the source build. Configure an **Orkas API Key** in **Settings → Models**, then click the microphone beside a composer. Allow microphone access when prompted. Audio is sent to Orkas for recognition and uses the key owner’s Orkas credits. Click again to stop, review the text, and send it yourself. If access was denied, enable the microphone in your system settings. --- ## Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent together Orkas runs the CLI agents you already have installed as local sessions, next to its own specialists — the coding agents **Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode**, and the personal agents **OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent**. The Commander hands each one the part it's best at and keeps one plan across all of them, so a single chat can fix the bug, review the change and draft the release note. Open-source tools such as HyperFrames plug in the same way. [Using Claude Code and Codex together →](https://orkas.ai/blog/claude-code-codex-together/?source=gh-orkas) --- ## Why Orkas - **A Commander that plans, delegates and does the rest** — it breaks down goals, picks the right agents, skills, connectors and tools, and handles analysis, writing, research and file work itself when no specialist is a better fit. - **Local-first by design** — conversations, files, knowledge bases and custom agents stay on your disk by default. Cloud sync is optional in the packaged app. With your own keys, model calls go straight from your machine to the provider; the built-in Orkas model runs through Orkas's managed model service. - **Any model, switch any time** — the Commander and built-in agents share one model setting: the built-in Orkas model, your own provider, or a local endpoint. External CLI agents keep their own model settings. - **Agents that get better** — each agent keeps private skills and memory. Background reviews examine new activity when the app is idle and can refine self-assessment, reusable methods and learned skills. - **Open source, no black box** — MIT licensed. Around it, Orkas adds a model-agnostic team for the work beyond code — research, content, video and more — with projects, to-dos and automations that keep it moving. [Orkas vs Claude Code →](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-claude-code/?source=gh-orkas) | | **Codex** | OpenAI's coding agent — in the terminal, your editor and the cloud. | Not either-or: Orkas runs Codex as one of its agents, next to Claude Code and OpenCode. The Commander can hand the coding to Codex and the review to another agent, then cover the non-code half of a release — docs, launch posts and videos. [Orkas vs Codex →](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-codex/?source=gh-orkas) | | **Claude Cowork** | Anthropic's agent for everyday work, now part of Claude — on desktop, web and mobile with a paid Claude plan. It runs in Anthropic's cloud by default and uses Claude models. | An open-source (MIT) alternative to Claude Cowork that's free to start, with 500 credits. Orkas runs its agents on your computer and keeps your data local by default, with the built-in Orkas model, your own provider keys or a local endpoint. The Commander can also bring in Claude Code, Codex and other CLI agents. The trade-off: Orkas needs your computer awake, while Cowork's cloud tasks can keep running without it. [Open-source Manus alternative →](https://orkas.ai/open-source-manus-alternative/?source=gh-orkas) | | **LangChain** | A developer framework/library for building LLM apps and agents — code-first, embedded in your own Python/JS app. | Orkas is a desktop app you direct through chat, not by writing orchestration code. Data stays local by default. | | **CrewAI** | A Python framework for orchestrating role-playing autonomous agents — you define crews and agents in code. | Orkas brings multi-agent orchestration into a desktop app, with projects, to-dos, automations and per-agent self-improvement built in. | | **OpenClaw** | A personal-agent platform with messaging integrations, multi-agent routing and sub-agents. | Orkas provides a desktop workspace for finished deliverables, with built-in specialists and coordination across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other CLI agents. OpenClaw can join that workflow as a CLI agent. | | **Hermes-Agent** | Nous Research's self-improving agent — one agent with memory and skills, available as a CLI, a messaging gateway and a desktop app. | Orkas coordinates a team: the Commander directs many specialists and other CLI agents, and Hermes-Agent plugs in as one of them. | **Orkas is for you if** you want a team of agents rather than one assistant, work that keeps moving across days, and your data, keys and agents on your own disk. **Not for you if** you just want a single all-purpose chatbot, or a pure code library to embed in your own app. **Choosing between coding agents?** [Codex vs OpenCode](https://orkas.ai/compare/codex-vs-opencode/?source=gh-orkas) · [Claude Code vs Codex vs OpenCode](https://orkas.ai/compare/claude-code-vs-codex-vs-opencode/?source=gh-orkas) · [Claude Code alternatives](https://orkas.ai/compare/claude-code-alternatives/?source=gh-orkas) **Full side-by-side comparisons →** [vs Claude Code](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-claude-code?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Codex](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-codex?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Cline](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-cline?source=gh-orkas) · [vs LangChain](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-langchain?source=gh-orkas) · [vs ChatGPT](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-chatgpt?source=gh-orkas) · [vs OpenClaw](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-openclaw?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Hermes-Agent](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-hermes-agent?source=gh-orkas) --- ## Quick start Want a packaged installer instead? See [Download](#download) above. To run from source — currently the way to run Orkas on Linux: **Requirements**: Node 22.12+ · macOS / Windows 10+ / glibc 2.34+ Linux x64 or arm64. Keep Python 3 and a C/C++ build toolchain available for the uncommon native-module source-build fallback. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Orkas-AI/Orkas.git cd Orkas ./run.sh # macOS / Linux run.cmd # Windows ``` Linux source runs require glibc 2.34+. Alpine and other musl-based distributions are not supported. Local speech transcription downloads and verifies the target-native whisper.cpp runtime and multilingual model during the first source launch. `run.sh` / `run.cmd` installs the locked npm dependency tree and prepares the pinned Python, uv, Node, embedding model (~95 MB), OfficeCLI, F
